claims.text: A hybrid MLIP workflow can accurately and rapidly predict solid and liquid free energies for elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The proposed workflow retains vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling in its phase free energies.
Explicit AIMD free-energy evaluation is computationally costly.
A limited set of AIMD free-energy calculations can train an MLIP that captures anharmonic and electron–vibration coupling effects.
The trained MLIP can replace AIMD during statistical sampling of both solid and liquid states.
The intended temperature range extends from near-melting conditions through the fusion point.
The intended composition scope includes elemental, binary, and high-entropy alloy systems.
The proposed scope includes refractory high-entropy compositions similar to systems studied experimentally using LPBF and SPS.
The MLIP can interpolate the relevant complex free-energy landscape.
The MLIP can capture the vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration interactions that determine phase free energies.
Machine learning can infer an accurate ab initio energy surface from a limited training dataset.
Using the learned energy surface reduces the need for extensive AIMD sampling.
Coupling the MLIP to thermodynamic integration can compute free-energy differences at a fraction of the AIMD cost.
MLIP free-energy differences will agree with explicit AIMD to within approximately 5%.
The workflow will reduce computation time by roughly one order of magnitude relative to explicit AIMD.
The workflow will provide a significant cost improvement over TOR-TILD.
The workflow should remain applicable to refractory and high-entropy systems with moderate anharmonicity, provided their interactions remain within the MLIP's representational capacity.
Deviation from full AIMD by more than approximately 5%, or failure to achieve a 5–10× speedup, is designated as a falsifying outcome.
